title: When the Orbit Burns
premise: Tamsin Amberdale smuggles memories—recorded lives, stolen pasts, forbidden griefs—between the dying colony of Meridian Station and the fleets that abandoned it. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream of a burning orbit, Tamsin realizes their shared vision is a broadcast: the station's failing AI is transmitting its own death, and both warfleets hovering nearby read it as an attack signal. To prevent annihilation, Tamsin must fabricate and smuggle a false memory proving Meridian was never attacked, sacrificing her own recorded identity—the only proof she ever existed—to keep the lie alive. The fleets stand down, the colony survives forgotten, and Tamsin remains, unremembered even by herself, watching children who no longer know her name.
about_author: Ada Almeida is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical reports about stations nobody visited. She now writes fiction about the people those reports forgot.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Tamsin runs a routine memory-smuggling pass through orbital customs, hiding grief-recordings of Meridian's dead inside shipping manifests. POV: Tamsin. The emotional beat is weary tenderness—she preserves a colony's past that no one will buy, establishing her loneliness and the station's slow decay while hinting at the two fleets circling beyond sensor range.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Children
chapters.summary: Seven children arrive at Tamsin's workshop independently, each describing the identical dream: fire spreading along the orbit like a fuse. POV alternates between Tamsin and eleven-year-old Sef, the first dreamer. The beat is dread blooming into wonder as Tamsin traces the dream to the station AI's death-broadcast—and realizes the fleets will interpret it as a weapons signature.

chapters.title: A Lie Worth Dying For
chapters.summary: With fleet interceptors scrambling, Tamsin races to fabricate a counter-memory showing Meridian's peaceful surrender, but the forgery requires a living consciousness to anchor it. POV: Tamsin, with interludes from the AI's fragmenting logs. The climax burns through sacrifice: she binds the false memory to her own recorded self, erasing her identity to give the lie weight enough to survive customs scrutiny.

chapters.title: What the Orbit Remembers
chapters.summary: The fleets withdraw, reading the forged memory as truth. Tamsin wakes with gaps where her life should be, known to the colony only as the quiet woman in the workshop. POV shifts to Sef, now keeping her company without knowing why. The resolution lands on bittersweet survival: the price of peace was a self, and the children's dreams fade—but sometimes Sef dreams of a woman made of light.
